chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamila al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Turayf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

I held the stirrup for the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), as he was about to mount. He raised his head and then smiled. I said: O Commander of the Faithful, I saw you raise your head and smile!

He said: Yes, O Asbagh. I held al-Shahba' (the Prophet's mule) for the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), and he raised his head toward the sky and smiled. I said: O Messenger of God, you raised your head toward the sky and smiled!

He said: O Ali, there is no one who mounts, then recites the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi), then says: "I seek forgiveness from God, besides whom there is no god, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I repent to Him. O God, forgive me my sins, for none forgives sins except You"
except that the Generous Master says: "O My angels, My servant knows that none forgives sins except Me, so bear witness that I have forgiven his sins."

key_terms.آية الكرسي: Ayat al-Kursi (Throne Verse) -- Quran 2:255, one of the most venerated verses
key_terms.استغفر الله: Astaghfirullah -- I seek God's forgiveness, a foundational formula of repentance
key_terms.الحي القيوم: Al-Hayy al-Qayyum -- The Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting; divine names from Ayat al-Kursi
key_terms.الركاب: Al-rikab -- the stirrup, used when mounting a riding animal
key_terms.الشهباء: Al-Shahba' -- name of the Prophet's mule

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when mounting a ride according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) told Imam Ali (AS) about a powerful supplication to recite after mounting a ride. According to this narration, whoever mounts and recites Ayat al-Kursi followed by a specific prayer for forgiveness (istighfar), God Himself announces to the angels that He has forgiven that servant's sins. This teaching was transmitted through the close relationship between Imam Ali and the Prophet, as both shared the gesture of raising the head and smiling upon mounting.
